newsitem.title: UK: Mark eases on crosses in Europe as dollar gains.
newsitem.headline: Mark eases on crosses in Europe as dollar gains.

text.p: The mark slipped on its European crosses in morning trade, hit mainly by a stronger dollar/mark following comments from Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke.
Welteke said earlier today a dollar/mark rate around 1.70 was supported by fundamental data. The dollar, already above 1.70 in early trade, tested levels above 1.7050 marks after his remarks.

The mark was also weaker on its crosses, particularly the lira, after Welteke also said sustainable low budget deficits were more important than the 3.0 percent deficit/GDP ratio target for monetary union.
However, analysts remained sceptical the Bundesbank and Germany had relaxed its strict interpretation of the three percent deficit/GDP ratio criteria.

"What he is saying is that 3.0 percent is still the target but you also have to stay there," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London. "The statement should be see as more mark positive."

Analysts said Welteke's emphasis on sustainable low budget deficits could be seen as a continuation of an Ecofin report early this week which called for more sustainable measures from Italy to control its spending.

"Everyone knows what the German attitude to Italy in EMU is. A trader would have to have a pretty short memory to buy the lira on this story," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International in London.
Mark/lira slipped to a session low of 984.55, its lowest level in almost four weeks. At 0830 GMT it stood at 985.25/55 against 988.50/9.00 late Tuesday.
The French franc was also firmer against the mark, lifted by the stronger dollar as well as a robust French February current account surplus of 19.2 billion francs, well above forecasts.
France's ruling centre-right coalition also continued to hold its lead in opinion polls ahead of the May 25/June 1 parliamentary election, providing franc support.
The franc earlier tested a near four-week high against the mark but eased back slightly to 3.3677/80 per mark by 0845 GMT. It stood at 3.3681/86 late on Tuesday.
The peseta also strengthened against the mark, bolstered by lower than expected inflation data as well as the robust dollar/mark.
Spanish April CPI came in at 1.7 percent year-on-year against an average forecast of 1.9 percent, reinforcing expectations of a near-term cut in the Spanish repo rate.

"The Bank of Spain is in an ideal scenario. Inflation is down and growth is coming along which is generally supportive of the peseta," Ken Wattret, international economist at Paribas, told Reuters Financial Television.
Mark/peseta fell to 84.42/43 from 84.62/65 late Tuesday.
The escudo also pulled ahead, trading at 100.40/43 per mark against 100.57/60.

The escudo was finding support from low inflation data released late Tuesday. Portugal's April CPI posted a 1.8 pct year-on-year gain against 2.5 percent in March. Average annual inflation, the government's yardstick, was 3.1 percent after 3.2 percent in March.
The Swedish crown was firmer, shrugging off earlier weakness on a press report quoting anonymous sources saying the Swedish government was opposed to EMU.
Mark/Swedish crown was trading at 4.4975/05 against 4.5100/30 late Tuesday.
-- Andrew Reierson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 6745
